answer: Ridge relic custody bond: each identity deposits one relic in the ridge archive and locks a 60-credit bond. A lantern auditor recomputes its custody chain from the ledger, checking each transfer signature; a break burns the bond. The first relic costs 34 to verify; each new relic is checked against all prior ones, so the k-th fake costs 34+6(k-1), the 1000th 6028, and 1000 fakes 3,031,000 plus 60,000 locked. A rented-relic ring fails: an archived hash cannot register twice, and the second filing burns both bonds. An honest identity pays 34 once and reclaims its bond on audit.
